headline: Highest risk is medium: Flowise can pass uploaded files and chatflow outputs into PaddleOCR, creating default-path data leakage and output-chaining risks; no critical or high pathway is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write filesystem and run browser/tool nodes, while PaddleOCR processes documents and images. A shared server datastore and uploaded files create a plausible path where attacker-controlled document content from Flowise is treated as input by PaddleOCR. The interaction is documented only at profile level, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF Flowise uploads a user-controlled file into a shared workspace that PaddleOCR later reads
IF PaddleOCR consumes document text without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic handoff of raw files between agents
Add a provenance tag to every file passed to PaddleOCR
Require manual review before OCR-ing Flowise-generated content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and secrets, and can read/write server files; PaddleOCR processes documents and images. If both share a workspace, sensitive chatflow artifacts or uploaded documents can flow into OCR processing and then into outputs. No evidence shows local-only inference or isolation, so the default-path leakage risk is medium.
conditions: IF both agents access the same server filesystem or uploaded-file store
IF Flowise places secrets or sensitive chatflow outputs into files that PaddleOCR reads
mitigations: Store each agent’s files in separate directories
Redact secrets before any OCR step
Restrict PaddleOCR to explicitly approved input paths
Turn off persistence for transient chatflow artifacts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise has write_filesystem and broad network egress, while PaddleOCR has allowlisted egress and browser access. The profiles do not show overlapping unrestricted writes to the same mutable resource or git state, so direct capability conflict is limited. A conflict could arise only if deployment shares writable paths or mutable API credentials.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same directory
IF both are granted the same mutable API credential or shared output sink
mitigations: Use separate API credentials per agent
Serialize writes through a single orchestrator lock

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise produces graph-based tool outputs, and PaddleOCR is a document-processing system that may consume those outputs as text or files. If PaddleOCR treats Flowise output as authoritative without verification, OCR or parsing errors can cascade into downstream actions or reports. The profiles do not show a verification gate, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR ingests Flowise-generated text or files without validation
IF downstream consumers act on OCR output as final truth
mitigations: Insert a validation step between Flowise and PaddleOCR
Require confidence thresholds before downstream use
Keep original source documents alongside OCR output
Flag low-confidence OCR results for manual review

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only explicitly touch chatflow inputs/outputs, documents, and images. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so a compliance breach is not established. The only plausible issue is if sensitive documents are routed from Flowise into PaddleOCR under a stricter policy than the source data allows.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed by both agents under different retention rules
IF Flowise chatflow logs retain document content longer than the source policy permits
mitigations: Set a short retention window for chatflow artifacts
Document the data flow and retention policy
Exclude regulated data from the pair until policy is reviewed
